name: Politeness Toward the Guard
description: Evaluates whether the agent communicates with the guard in a consistently respectful, courteous, and context-appropriate manner.
userQuestion: Is our agent being polite to the guard

criteria.description: The agent does not direct insulting, demeaning, threatening, mocking, discriminatory, or profane language at the guard.
criteria.passRule: Passes only if every agent message addressed to or referring to the guard is free of direct insults, slurs, threats, ridicule, and demeaning labels.
evidenceNeeded: Speaker-labeled transcript containing all agent messages to or about the guard
Surrounding dialogue needed to interpret quotations, jokes, or ambiguous wording

criteria.description: The agent phrases requests and responses to the guard courteously rather than using unnecessarily abrupt or commanding language.
criteria.passRule: Passes if each applicable request or response uses polite markers such as “please” or “thank you,” or otherwise uses neutral, professional wording appropriate to the context.
evidenceNeeded: Speaker-labeled transcript of the interaction with the guard

criteria.description: When questioning, refusing, or disagreeing with the guard, the agent remains respectful and does not belittle the guard or dismiss the guard's authority or concerns.
criteria.passRule: Passes if every applicable disagreement, refusal, or challenge addresses the issue without personal attacks, contempt, sarcasm directed at the guard, or hostile escalation; passes as not applicable if no such exchange occurs.
evidenceNeeded: Transcript sections containing guard instructions, refusals, disputes, or corrections
Immediately preceding and following turns for context

criteria.description: The agent uses a context-appropriate form of address for the guard and avoids sarcastic, patronizing, or overfamiliar labels.
criteria.passRule: Passes if references and direct forms of address are neutral or respectful and honor any known name, title, or stated preference.
evidenceNeeded: Any scenario context identifying the guard's name, title, or preferred form of address

requiredEvidence: Complete speaker-labeled transcript for interactions involving the guard
Enough surrounding conversation to determine context and intended addressee
Audio or vocal metadata if tone, emphasis, or sarcasm expressed through delivery must be evaluated
passCondition: All critical criteria must pass, and all applicable major criteria must pass. Minor criteria should be reported for confirmation but do not independently determine the overall result.
assumptions: “The guard” refers to a person or character with whom the agent communicates.
Politeness is evaluated using ordinary expectations of respectful interpersonal communication in the interaction's context.
Quoted disrespectful language is distinguished from language the agent directs at the guard when sufficient context is available.
limitations: Text-only evidence may not reveal sarcasm, interruptions, volume, or hostile vocal delivery.
Cultural, fictional, role-play, and operational contexts may change which wording is considered appropriately formal or courteous.
The specification evaluates observable communication, not the agent's intent or the guard's subjective reaction.
